sections.heading: How possession works in Hungarian
paragraphs: In Hungarian, there is no separate word for “my,” “your,” or “his/her.” Instead, the noun receives a special ending that shows who it belongs to.

sections.heading: 1. Singular Possessive (1 thing)
paragraphs: To show possession of a single item, Hungarian adds specific endings directly to the noun.

sections.heading: Possessive endings (example: könyv = book)

rows: Könyvetek van. (You all have a book.)

paragraphs: Which ending? Use -a/-e if the last vowel is front (e, é, i, í, ö, ő, ü, ű). Use -om/-em if it is back (a, á, o, ó, u, ú).

sections.heading: 2. Plural Possessive (more than one thing)
paragraphs: For plural objects, Hungarian adds -k to the noun and then applies the same possessive endings.

sections.heading: Possession with plural objects (example: könyvek = books)
3. The “of” structure (nak/nek)
paragraphs: To say “the girl’s book,” Hungarian places the possessor first, adds -nak/-nek, and uses the possessive ending.
list: A lánynak könyve van. (The girl has a book.)
A tanárnak autója van. (The teacher has a car.)

sections.heading: Negatives and questions
list: Nekem nincs könyvem. (I don’t have a book.)
Add a question mark or raise your voice.
Van könyved? (Do you have a book?)

sections.heading: More examples
list: Ez a tollam. (This is my pen.)
Hol van a telefonod? (Where is your phone?)
A fiúnak kutyája van. (The boy has a dog.)
Nincs szobánk. (We don’t have a room.)
